summary: Updated scapy package fixes security vulnerabilities
details:
This update fixes security issues:
CVE-2025-71463:
Scapy before 2.7.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in
the load_session function that allows attackers to execute code by
supplying a malicious pickle session file. Attackers can trick users
into loading a crafted .pkl.gz file via the -s option or conf.session,
executing embedded Python code through __reduce__().
CVE-2026-128237:
Scapy before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in
BER_num_dec() and BERcodec_OID.do_dec() that allows remote attackers to
exhaust CPU by supplying oversized OID arcs. Attackers can send
ASN.1/BER data with many base-128 continuation bytes to cause quadratic
CPU consumption or an uncaught ValueError crash on Python 3.11+.
CVE-2026-128238:
Scapy before 2.8.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in
the BER/ASN.1 decoder in scapy/asn1/ber.py that allows unauthenticated
remote attackers to crash parsing applications. Attackers can send a
single 833-byte packet with 250 nested ASN.1 SEQUENCE structures to
trigger an unhandled RecursionError, terminating TLS, SNMP, X.509, or
LDAP parsers even with safe=True.
